descriptionChirho: Engraving or carved decorative work, a nominal derivative of patach II (to engrave). Used for the engravings on the priestly breastplate stones inscribed like a signet seal with the names of Israel's tribes (Exod 28:11,21,36; 39:6,14,30), for carved ornamental work on the walls and doors of Solomon's temple (1 Kgs 6:29), for the engraving on the stone set before Joshua the high priest (Zech 3:9), for the carved work destroyed in the temple (Ps 74:6), and for craftsman's engravings in Chronicles (2 Chr 2:7,14). Arabic naqsh (engraving/inscription), German Gravierung (engraving), Spanish grabado (engraving), Hindi khudai (carving), Korean jogak/saegim (sculpture/engraving). All auto-clusters are inflectional variants (singular, plural, construct, with suffixes) of the same noun denoting decorative incised work on stone, metal, or wood.
